audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill on all seven rows against the content layer and packet chart's Karma/Karma/Karma/Skill/Zoe/Zoe/Zoe. Separately, the content whys[] array was offset by one row: whys[3] described her level-6 spike under the Levels 4-5 row, whys[4] described her first item under the Level 6 row, and whys[5] described late-game roaming under the First-item row.
audit.why: Inner Flame at 950 out-ranges both Paddle Star! and Sleepy Trouble Bubble at 800, so levels 1-3 are Karma's. Levels 4-5 are even on whether the bubble lands. Portal Jump at 11s is the level-6 change; the one-shot combo is the first-item change; roaming picks are the late-game one.
audit.corrected: Full rows 0-2 to Karma and 4-6 to Zoe; whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] rewritten so each describes its own row.
sources: enemyKit Q/E range 800, E cd 18/17/16/15/14, R cd 11/8/5

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and mid both described Zoe's ultimate as 'a burst-and-reset combo through sleep bubble'.
audit.why: Portal Jump does one thing: blink to a nearby position for 1 second, then blink back, on 11/8/5s. It resets nothing and adds no damage — what it buys her is casting Paddle Star! from outside your range and returning before you can answer.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid, whys[4] and phases[4].why all rewritten on what Portal Jump actually does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer twice called Zoe melee — 'her melee-range autos', 'Zoe's melee-reliant auto-attacks' — and referred to Karma's damage as a 'Q-E poke combo'. breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Zoe is a ranged mage whose Q and E both reach 800; Karma's E is Inspiration, a pure shield with no damage. The decisive interaction is Sleepy Trouble Bubble: drowsy, then asleep, MR reduced while asleep, and the first source of damage that breaks the sleep is doubled up to a cap — which is why the Mantra-E shield belongs on the wake-up hit, and why Karma, with no dash, must hold Flash for the bubble rather than the damage.
audit.corrected: Melee claims removed, 'Q-E poke' removed, and breakdown.cooldowns now carries the bubble at 18s/14s, Paddle Star! at 8.5s and Portal Jump at 11s with its 1-second return.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fourteen lintFindings: ten MISGENDER fields calling Zoe 'he/his/him', two COPY_PASTE_BLEED bullets, and the cooldowns field.
audit.why: champ-gender lists zoe as she/her; the template was written for a male enemy and only the name was swapped.
audit.corrected: All misgendered fields in scope fixed (tldr, phases[3].why, breakdown.mid, breakdown.wave, four dos/donts titles, report[0].t, report[4].t). Both bleed bullets rewritten to their titles.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are clearly Karma's: your Q-E poke combo out-ranges Zoe's melee-reliant auto-attacks and her Q sleep bubble is a slow, dodgeable skillshot at this stage, so you can chip her down every wave without real risk. She has no way to punish your range advantage and is forced into a passive farming pattern. By levels 4-5 it shifts into a genuine skill matchup as Zoe starts landing bubble-into-auto combos more consistently and her damage output ramps up, meaning careful positioning around her Q sightlines matters far more than before.

edits.before: Level 6 flips decisively toward Zoe: her ultimate grants a full burst-and-reset combo through a landed sleep bubble that can delete Karma in one rotation, and her damage output now clearly outpaces your poke-and-shield kit in a straight fight. This trend continues through her first item spike, where her one-shot combo becomes even more threatening and her stolen-summoner tech (grabbing Flash or Exhaust off a kill) lets her snowball the lane further. Play significantly safer through this stretch — avoid walking into any sightline where her Q bubble could land clean, since getting slept means eating her entire combo.
